proof: Every countably infinite locally finite p-group embeds in the canonical nil-adjoint Golod group from the stated presentation. Separately each is a quotient of a subgroup of an infinite finitely generated residually finite classical homogeneous Golod p-group. The quotient statement does not identify a residually finite subgroup embedding for arbitrary targets.

Each longitudinal generator rotates the immediate child after a departure with label 1 at precisely its infinitely many assigned levels. Prefix antichains make those portraits independent. The actual original Rozhkov definition uses a subset D and combines accompanying permutations over all departure symbols, so the root cycle and one assigned generator per level give transitivity. For finitely many directed generators, a missing label at a chosen depth eliminates the side root action there, putting all sections into a common finite elementary abelian tail group. The faithful wreath decomposition proves local finiteness on the infinite tree.

The increasing cyclic wreath envelope puts every element in its derived subgroup by the exact wrap-controlled coordinate commutator. The characteristic-p augmentation ideal is absolutely stable nil because the finite supports lie in finite p-subgroup algebras; induction on a central order-p element kills their augmentation ideals. The relative elementary group embeds the derived subgroup through the exact ordered two-unit product identity, and the finite generator-difference subalgebra is nil and nonnilpotent.

The published stable-nil embedding construction admits the stated all-field refinement by one prime-field polynomial/matrix seed, external scalar extension of the finite-row ideal and its finite corner with square-zero kernel. This makes the difference algebra absolutely nil. Hammoudi's homogeneous J⊂I cover retains finite generators and has separating finite degree quotients. Pull back the embedded target to get the required section. This answers existential Problem 21.131 and does not settle the distinct whole-group Problem 13.55.
